title: Cuba Exhausts All Fuel Reserves; 20–22 Hour Blackouts as Energy Crisis Peaks
detail: Cuba's Energy and Mines Minister Vicente de la O Levy publicly declared on May 14, 2026 that the island had exhausted all fuel oil and diesel reserves. Nationwide electrical blackouts were running 20–22 hours per day, affecting hospitals, food distribution, water pumping, and transportation. The crisis was a direct consequence of Trump's Executive Order 14380 (January 29, 2026), which blocked oil shipments to Cuba and threatened secondary tariffs on any country supplying the island. Russia had delivered one tanker that arrived in late March 2026, but subsequent shipments faced OFAC blocking or White House case-by-case review. Cuba's acute fuel crisis in May 2026 surpassed the severity of the 1990s 'Special Period' following Soviet collapse in immediate daily impact, though Cuba's pre-crisis infrastructure was already deteriorated from years of economic contraction since 2021. The energy collapse was cited by both Cuban and US officials as the backdrop for CIA Director Ratcliffe's arrival in Havana on the same day.

title: CIA Director Ratcliffe Visits Havana in Rare High-Level US–Cuba Contact
detail: CIA Director John Ratcliffe traveled to Havana on May 14–15, 2026, meeting with Raúl Guillermo Rodríguez Castro ('Raulito', Raúl Castro's grandson and a senior Cuban intelligence official), Interior Minister Lázaro Álvarez Casas, and the head of Cuban intelligence. The visit was the first by a sitting CIA director to Cuba in decades. It was preceded by a secret February 2026 meeting between Rodríguez Castro and Secretary of State Marco Rubio in St. Kitts. Ratcliffe delivered Trump's message that the US would 'seriously engage' on economic and security matters only if Cuba made 'fundamental changes' — including releasing political prisoners, ending support for adversary nations, and providing transparency on biological weapons research. Cuba objected to remaining on the State Sponsors of Terrorism list and argued it posed no national security threat to the US. The Havana visit represented the highest-level US intelligence contact with Cuba since the failed 2015–2017 Obama normalization era, taking place as the island's fuel reserves reached zero and daily blackouts exceeded 20 hours — conditions that gave the US maximum coercive leverage over the negotiations.
